22.t: Working with data: double bonds and melting point
q: Using the saturated fatty acids only, describe the effect of chain length on melting point.
Longer chains have higher melting points: 12 carbons 44 °C, 18 carbons 70 °C.
Explain why only fatty acids with 18 carbons should be used to judge the effect of double bonds.
Chain length also affects melting point, so it must be kept the same (controlled).
Oleic and elaidic acid both have one double bond. Explain the 32 °C difference in their melting points.

The cis double bond puts a kink in oleic acid, so the chains cannot pack closely and the forces between them are weak. The trans bond keeps the chain almost straight, so elaidic acid packs like a saturated fat and is solid at room temperature.
Identify which fatty acids would be liquid in a fish living at 4 °C.
Linoleic and linolenic acid (oleic acid melts at 13 °C, so it is solid at 4 °C).
Suggest why the seeds of plants from cold places store oils rich in linolenic acid.
These oils stay liquid at low temperatures, so enzymes can reach them and the energy can be released quickly for germination.
